articles.title: Trump sued over service selling faster access to Truth Social posts

articles.title: Long a dream, it's now real: a fast and accurate TB test that doesn't need phlegm
articles.description: TB tests use phlegm — not the easiest thing to get or work with. It takes time for results. And there can be false negatives and positives. A new test is more accurate and takes less than half an hour.

articles.title: The Trump administration has secretly rewritten nuclear safety rules
articles.description: The rewrite was done to speed up the construction of a new generation of nuclear reactors. Critics warn it could compromise safety and public trust.

articles.title: To win over working-class voters, Democrats need to stop talking about democracy
articles.description: Working-class voters have moved away from the Democratic Party. Winning them back is key to the party's future, a new reports shows. But first, the messaging has to change.

articles.title: U.S. and Iran announce an initial deal to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz
articles.description: The deal is a major breakthrough in the conflict that set the Middle East aflame and shook the global economy. However, it did not resolve critical issues set aside for further negotiations.

articles.title: Supreme Court upholds birthright citizenship on constitutional grounds
articles.description: The decision firmly rejected the executive order that Trump issued on the first day of his second term.

articles.title: DOJ is investigating former congressman George Santos for insider trading on Kalshi
articles.description: The disgraced former congressman allegedly bet on whether he would appear at the State of the Union address, prompting federal investigations.

articles.title: Former ethics lawyer says Trump's crypto poses 'clear conflict of interest'
articles.description: Former White House ethics lawyer Richard Painter says President Trump "stands alone" in having substantial financial conflicts of interest and that, "for every other executive branch official, it would be a violation."

articles.title: Trump further guts Education Dept. by shifting oversight of special ed, civil rights
articles.description: The moves to the federal departments of Health and Human Services and Justice, respectively, would further dismantle an agency that President Donald Trump has vowed to close.

articles.title: Iran's supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, has been killed
articles.description: The Iranian government has declared 40 days of national mourning after Khamenei was killed in a U.S.-Israeli attack on Saturday.

articles.title: Federal judge finds Trump violated free speech by ordering NPR defunded
articles.description: A U.S. District Court judge found that President Trump's executive order calling for the defunding of NPR and PBS violated the First Amendment.

articles.title: Over 4 million people are no longer receiving food aid amid sweeping changes to SNAP
articles.description: SNAP, also known as food stamps, has seen a rapid and consistent participation decline since last July. The drop comes as the program faces historic cuts and changes.

articles.title: In the Southeast, power company money flows to news sites that attack their critics
articles.description: Alabama Power and Florida Power & Light hired the consulting firm Matrix to help shape their fortunes. Matrix funded six sites that covered politics, filling a void left by the decline of local news.

articles.title: Justice Department subpoenas New York Times reporters over Air Force One reporting
articles.description: The Times says federal agents turned up on the doorsteps of several of its journalists to force grand jury testimony next week over their coverage of the Air Force One plane gifted to Trump by Qatar.

articles.title: Corporation for Public Broadcasting says it's shutting down
articles.description: The Corporation for Public Broadcasting, which funnels federal money to public media stations, says it's winding down operations after President Trump signed a law rescinding all funding.

articles.title: Trump to get 'routine annual' medical exam 7 months after last visit to Walter Reed
articles.description: White House boasts Trump's "excellent health" as questions loom over the medical reality of the oldest inaugurated president.

articles.title: Rage-giving, innovation and cuts: How public media has survived without federal funds
articles.description: A year after President Trump signed a law ending six decades of federal funding of public media, it's a time of reinvention, innovation and clear anxiety at public tv and radio stations nationwide.

articles.title: Elon Musk threatens to sue over Gibney documentary's "space lasers" claim
articles.description: The tech billionaire's attorney has put documentarian Alex Gibney and his production company on legal notice, claiming the Oscar-winning director defamed Musk in his nearly four-hour documentary.

articles.title: USPS 'carefully reviewing' whistleblower claim on plan for Trump's mail voting order
articles.description: A whistleblower says the U.S. Postal Service is rushing out an online system for President Trump's push to restrict mail voting that could "derail" the midterm election if courts allow it to proceed.

articles.title: Exclusive: GM, Pepsi, Disney, others scrub some DEI references from investor reports
articles.description: Some companies have announced diversity rollbacks — but many more are deleting or softening language from their investor disclosures, an NPR analysis finds.

articles.title: To keep AI out of her classroom, this high school English teacher went analog
articles.description: Forth Worth teacher Chanea Bond says sticking with pen and paper keeps generative artificial intelligence out of her American literature classes.

articles.title: DOJ memo stokes fear among disability advocates of a return to institutionalization
articles.description: The Justice Department's opinion challenges civil rights protections that have long treated the institutionalization of disabled Americans as a last resort.

articles.title: The U.S. military says it will blockade Iranian ports as Iran peace talks collapse
articles.description: After talks between the U.S. and Iran collapsed, President Trump said the U.S. will "blockade" the Strait of Hormuz. The U.S. military said it would blockade ships entering or exiting Iranian ports.

articles.title: Trump signs new orders targeting birthright citizenship, weeks after Supreme Court ruling
articles.description: President Trump is once again attempting to put restrictions on who is automatically guaranteed citizenship after being born in the U.S., just weeks after the Supreme Court struck down his attempt to end birthright citizenship.

articles.title: Iran rejects Trump's proposal to end the war and lays out 5 conditions
articles.description: Iran says no to President Trump's ceasefire plan and publicized a counterproposal that includes war reparations and Iranian sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: House Democrats accuse Trump of 'hijacking' America's 250th birthday for his own gain
articles.description: A 55-page report from House Democrats accuses Freedom 250 of America's birthday celebrations for profit, using questionable fundraising methods. Watchdog groups had already sounded alarms.

articles.title: A suspect identified in correspondents' dinner shooting
articles.description: A suspect has been identified in the Saturday night shooting at the White House Correspondents Dinner. President Trump and several cabinet members were safely rushed from the event.

articles.title: Yemen's Houthis capture a Red Sea island in threat to shipping
articles.description: Iranian-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen have captured a strategic island in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. The move threatens Saudi oil exports through a key commercial lane. And Saudi Arabia said it shut down a major oil pipeline as a precaution after it came under attack.

articles.title: Dolly Parton, one of country music's most singular performers, has died at age 80
articles.description: The artist was a star performer in country music and went on to become one of the genre's most recognizable and universally adored ambassadors to broader popular culture.

articles.title: A melting glacier contributed to the deadly Nepal floods. We can expect more like this
articles.description: As the climate continues to warm, scientists warn that the frequency of disasters like the floods in Nepal will increase.

articles.title: Trump allies vote to weaken protections for historic sites — not just in D.C.
articles.description: A council packed with Trump appointees wants to rewrite historic preservation rules. Critics say that could help him build his D.C. arch faster — and endanger important sites across the country.

articles.title: Fed's Kevin Warsh warns inflation is too high, sparking bets rate hikes are coming
articles.description: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh reiterated his commitment to fighting inflation in a major speech — raising expectations that rate hikes may be coming, though he did not clearly spell out a path going forward.

articles.title: ICE is now funded through end of Trump's term, raising worries about oversight
articles.description: The GOP bill signed by President Trump provides roughly $70 billion for immigration enforcement, even as Democrats warn that Congress has ceded its oversight role with the legislation.

articles.title: Trump officials propose sweeping changes to the census that would reshape voting maps
articles.description: A Trump census proposal would stop asking about race and exclude millions of U.S. residents from a count that the 14th Amendment says must include the "whole number of persons in each state."

articles.title: NPR defends its journalism after senior editor says it has lost the public's trust
articles.description: A veteran NPR editor publicly questions whether the public radio network has, in its push for greater diversity and representation, overlooked conservative viewpoints.

articles.title: Anthropic sues the Trump administration over 'supply chain risk' label
articles.description: The Pentagon told suppliers they can't use Anthropic's artificial intelligence tools after the company said it would not let its tech be used for autonomous weapons and mass domestic surveillance.

articles.title: U.S. and Iran peace deal within reach, Pakistan's prime minister says
articles.description: The U.S. and Iran appeared closer to reaching a peace deal on Friday, as a sequence of social media posts signaled progress. President Trump had previously been amping up his rhetoric against Iran.

articles.title: On her new album, Kacey Musgraves returns home, to the 'Middle of Nowhere'
articles.description: Before making her upcoming sixth album, the country star returned to her small-town Texas home and discovered the power of in-between spaces. "I found a lot of clarity there," she says.

articles.title: In real-world test, an AI model did better than doctors at diagnosing patients
articles.description: Researchers evaluated how well an AI model could diagnose and make decisions about patient care in the ER.

articles.title: What to know about cyclosporiasis, the intestinal illness hitting the U.S.
articles.description: A surge of cases of the intestinal illness that causes diarrhea and fatigue has been detected in 34 states. Here's how what to do if you suspect you have it and how to avoid infection.

articles.title: Empty seats, socialism and Trump dominate the Republican midterm convention
articles.description: The two day Republican convention in Dallas showcased the party's biggest asset in trying to win competitive midterm races and its greatest obstacle: President Trump.

articles.title: Justice Department publishes some missing Epstein files related to Trump
articles.description: The Justice Department has published additional Epstein files related to allegations that President Trump sexually abused a minor after an NPR investigation found dozens of pages were withheld.

articles.title: DOT cranks up its campaign to strip bike lane references from federal websites
articles.description: Transportation officials have removed a growing list of safety materials that mention bike lanes from federal websites. Safety advocates warn that's undermining proven measures for reducing crashes.

articles.title: Bezos orders deep job cuts at 'Washington Post'
articles.description: The Washington Post embarked on severe cuts despite appeals by the newsroom to owner Jeff Bezos. The paper is to narrow its focus largely to politics and national security.

articles.title: Trump's VA killed a home loan program. Vets are now losing their homes because of it
articles.description: Foreclosures on VA loans are at their highest level in a decade. VA has a fix but it is months away and could still leave vets worse off than most other homeowners.

articles.title: Immigration courts are using a new tactic to speed up deportations
articles.description: The Justice Department is moving up the court hearings for hundreds of immigrants and scheduling them for mass hearings. If they don't show up, they could be ordered deported.

articles.title: At 'No Kings' rallies, anti-Trump protesters speak out against ICE 'cruelty,' Iran war
articles.description: Organizers behind No Kings, a network of progressive groups, say millions turned out in cities and towns across the country and abroad to speak out against the Trump administration's actions.

articles.title: Trump signs preliminary agreement with Iran, after releasing details
articles.description: The Trump administration shared the details of the preliminary agreement to end the war with Iran on Wednesday. President Trump later said he had signed it, during a dinner with French President Emmanuel Macron.

articles.title: A fragile U.S.-Iran ceasefire shows cracks as attacks continue across the region
articles.description: Iran and the U.S. and Israel said they would suspend strikes but countries in the region continued to report attacks and Israel said it would not stop its assault in Lebanon.

articles.title: AI music is flooding streaming platforms. But listeners like it less and less
articles.description: Music fans are becoming increasingly uncomfortable with AI songs, according to a recent study.

articles.title: Read the full text of Trump's preliminary U.S.-Iran agreement to end the war
articles.description: Here is the text of the memorandum of understanding that was signed Wednesday by President Trump and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, as well as Pakistan's prime minister.

articles.title: Trump touts Iran breakthrough but details remain unclear
articles.description: President Trump announced the unfinalized deal on social media after talks with Israel and other allies. Iran did not officially confirm the deal, and state media contradicted parts of it.

articles.title: A brief history of NPR funding : The Indicator from Planet Money
articles.description: Where does NPR get its funding? Today on the show, we open our books and share a brief history of public radio. And we learn what's at stake with President Trump's executive order to cut off federal funding to NPR. Under NPR's protocol for reporting on itself, no corporate official or news executive reviewed this story before it was posted publicly. articles.title: The U.S. and Iran agree to a 'road map' for a final deal, mediators say
articles.description: Qatar and Pakistan said the talks made "encouraging progress" despite a rocky start after Trump made threats to "hit Iran very hard again" while the U.S. and Iranian negotiators met in Switzerland.

articles.title: Environmental groups sue government to stop a big change to the Endangered Species Act
articles.description: By altering the definition of the word "harm" as used by the Endangered Species Act, the Trump administration may limit how wildlife is protected in the United States. Environmental groups are suing.

articles.title: A tech worker in China is laid off and replaced by AI. Is it legal?
articles.description: A tech worker in eastern China's Hangzhou city was dismissed after his job was replaced by AI. An appeals court in the city has ruled the dismissal unlawful.

articles.title: Supreme Court allows Trump's ballroom construction to continue
articles.description: The ruling comes after months of back-and-forth between the Trump administration and the National Trust for Historic Preservation.

articles.title: Alien Terrorist Removal Court deports legal US resident to Afghanistan in first-ever case
articles.description: Nazira Haji Zada, a lawful permanent resident, conceded to being an "alien terrorist." It marks the first case in the Alien Terrorist Removal Court.

articles.title: Supreme Court majority seems inclined to rule against Trump on birthright citizenship
articles.description: The majority seemed skeptical of the Trump administration's argument on birthright citizenship, appearing ready to rule in favor of upholding automatic citizenship for babies born on U.S. soil.

articles.title: Overworked and understaffed: Special ed teachers turn to AI for help
articles.description: A fast-growing number of special educators nationwide are using AI to create customized education plans. Despite the risks, some research shows it could improve the quality of teachers' work.

articles.title: NPR trims jobs in newsroom overhaul as it confronts era without public funding
articles.description: NPR is offering buyouts to journalists as it overhauls its newsroom, with the threat of layoffs to follow. Two recent gifts totaling $113 million are primarily dedicated to NPR's tech infrastructure.

articles.title: Families of USS Lincoln crew say Trump should be 'ashamed' of conditions on board
articles.description: President Trump said the USS Abraham Lincoln deployment is "not nearly long enough." A family member of a sailor on board that ship said those comments are shameful.

articles.title: U.S. seizes Iranian cargo ship in Strait of Hormuz
articles.description: The U.S. has taken custody of an Iranian-flagged cargo ship in the Strait of Hormuz after firing on its engine room, President Trump said in a post on social media.

articles.title: Canada hits back at the U.S. with tariffs as the countries' trade fight escalates
articles.description: The measures come after President Trump imposed 50% tariffs on many Canadian goods and threatened more after trade talks broke down on Friday.

articles.title: Spain is the 2026 World Cup champion, defeating Argentina for its 2nd title
articles.description: Spain's run to the title was a defensive masterclass, with wins over four of the world's top ten teams. They are the first World Cup champion to win the title while only conceding a single goal.

articles.title: André 3000 opens up about 'New Blue Sun,' his daring new solo album
articles.description: Out now, the outrageous half of OutKast about talks about his first album in 17 years, his wild ayahuasca trip and why he gets so many requests to play flute at funerals.

articles.title: Where is 'Harry's House' anyway? Harry Styles explains
articles.description: The pop star has spent a life on the go, so the pandemic offered him a rare chance for reflection, to separate the person from the pop star. Also, of course, to record a new album.

articles.title: Pro-Trump counties now have far higher COVID death rates. Misinformation is to blame
articles.description: An analysis by NPR shows that since the vaccine rollout, counties that voted heavily for Donald Trump have had more than twice the COVID mortality rates of those that voted for Joe Biden.

articles.title: 'White Lotus' creator Mike White finds wide success after 25 years in the margins
articles.description: As the second season of HBO's The White Lotus comes to a close, creator Mike White reflects on how it examines the dark side of sex, and how at its heart is a mix of Laverne & Shirley and Survivor .

articles.title: James Cameron wants everyone to see 'Avatar 2' in theaters
articles.description: NPR's A Martinez speaks with Director James Cameron about "Avatar: The Way of Water," the long-awaited sequel to his 2009 science-fiction blockbuster, "Avatar."

articles.title: 'Live free and die?' The sad state of U.S. life expectancy
articles.description: A decade after a landmark report on Americans' shorter lives, the problem has only gotten worse. Unlike other wealthy nations, U.S. life expectancy has not bounced back from the pandemic.

articles.title: That smiling LinkedIn profile face might be a computer-generated fake
articles.description: Stanford researchers uncovered more than 1,000 of these LinkedIn profiles. A technology that has been used to promote misinformation online has now entered the corporate world.

articles.title: 'Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow' review: This video game novel is a winner
articles.description: Gabrielle Zevin's beautifully written novel Tomorrow and Tomorrow and Tomorrow tells the story of two childhood friends who become legendary names in the world of video game design.

articles.title: Nintendo's Miyamoto says inspiration comes from his childhood experiences in nature
articles.description: NPR's A Martinez speaks to Nintendo game director Shigeru Miyamoto about the ways in which his games have engaged players for more than 30 years.

articles.title: Homelessness in the U.S. hit a record high last year as pandemic aid ran out
articles.description: The jump is 12% more than the year before and came as rents and inflation skyrocketed. The increase was driven by families and those who lost housing for the first time.

articles.title: Starbucks workers have unionized at record speed; many fear retaliation now
articles.description: More than 300 Starbucks stores have held union elections in less than a year, a remarkable feat. But now workers blame "scorched-earth" union busting by Starbucks for a slowdown in the momentum.

articles.title: NPR Music's 100 Best Songs of 2021
articles.description: Think of the best songs of 2021 as a playlist catering to the most basic human urges. Within it, booties were called, muffins were buttered and bloody revenge was contemplated. It was quite a year.

articles.title: What is 'quiet quitting,' and how it may be a misnomer for setting boundaries at work
articles.description: Quiet quitting is taking over TikTok as a new workplace trend popular with Gen Z. However, it may be a misnomer for setting healthy boundaries in the workplace.

articles.title: 6 things we've learned about how the pandemic disrupted learning
articles.description: As a third pandemic school year draws to a close, new research offers the clearest accounting yet of the pandemic's academic toll.

articles.title: How 'modern-day slavery' in the Congo powers the rechargeable battery economy
articles.description: Phone and electric car batteries are made with cobalt mined in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Cobalt Red author Siddharth Kara describes the conditions for workers as a "horror show."

articles.title: NPR names tech executive Katherine Maher to lead in turbulent era
articles.description: Incoming NPR CEO Katherine Maher has a background in tech and world affairs. She says the network's mission fits neatly with her advocacy of the free flow of information in expanding democracy.

articles.title: Dolly Parton has made a rock & roll album — with a little help from her friends
articles.description: NPR's Juana Summers speaks to country music legend Dolly Parton about her new album Rockstar .

articles.title: Supreme Court guts affirmative action, effectively ending race-conscious admissions
articles.description: The decision reverses decades of precedent upheld over the years by narrow court majorities that included Republican-appointed justices.

articles.title: Poll shows majority of Americans see an 'invasion' at the southern border
articles.description: A new NPR/Ipsos poll shows that half of Americans say there's an "invasion" at the southern border. And that false and misleading claims about migrants are taking hold, particularly with Republicans.

articles.title: America's fastest-growing sport is a cross of tennis, pingpong and badminton
articles.description: With 4.8 million people now playing, pickleball is ready for the big time.

articles.title: PFAS 'forever chemicals' are everywhere. Here's what you should know about them
articles.description: PFAS are all around us, so how do we navigate a world filled with harmful chemicals? We speak to an expert who guides us through what PFAS are, why they're a problem, and what can be done about them.

articles.title: Supreme Court overturns Roe v. Wade, ending right to abortion upheld for decades
articles.description: The U.S. Supreme Court has overturned the constitutional right to an abortion, reversing Roe v. Wade, the court's five-decade-old decision that guaranteed a woman's right to obtain an abortion.

articles.title: Turnout among young voters was the second highest for a midterm in past 30 years
articles.description: About 27% of voters between the ages of 18-29 cast a ballot in the midterm election this year, according to an early estimate.

articles.title: Therapy by chatbot? The promise and challenges in using AI for mental health
articles.description: Some companies and researchers think smart computers might eventually help with provider shortages in mental health, and some consumers are already turning to chatbots to build "emotional resilience."

articles.title: Roy Wood Jr. says he's leaving 'The Daily Show' but he doesn't hold a grudge
articles.description: Late night TV has seen a recent exodus of non-white stars — from Desus and Mero and Ziwe to Trevor Noah himself.

articles.title: Elon Musk says NPR's 'state-affiliated media' label might not have been accurate
articles.description: In a series of emails with an NPR reporter, the CEO of Twitter suggested that the designation is being re-examined, but it has not yet been removed.

articles.title: 'The voice we woke up to': Bob Edwards, longtime 'Morning Edition' host, dies at 76
articles.description: Edwards, a consummate newsman, hosted NPR's morning show for more than two decades. "He sort of set the tone and the bar for all of us," says one former NPR executive.

articles.title: With 'Bewitched,' Laufey hopes listeners can escape
articles.description: NPR's A Martinez speaks with singer Laufey about making jazz more accessible to younger generations. She has a new album called Bewitched .

articles.title: This Palestinian American professor leans on his Quaker faith during conflict
articles.description: Here's how one professor holds on to the pacifism and silent meditation espoused by Quakers when the world feels like it's on fire.

articles.title: Electric cars have a road trip problem, even for the secretary of energy
articles.description: A road trip I took with Energy Secretary Jennifer Granholm confirmed one thing: The U.S. is wrestling with an inadequate charging network (unless you're a Tesla driver).

articles.title: Movie extras worry they'll be replaced by AI. Hollywood is already doing body scans
articles.description: Five background actors told NPR they had to undergo face and body digital scans while on TV and movie sets. The use of digital replicas is a sticking point in the ongoing strikes in Hollywood.

articles.title: Bethesda's Starfield is a fabulous playable space opera with a forgettable story
articles.description: In the massively-anticipated game Starfield, space exploration is its own reward. Good thing too, because the slow storyline isn't the star of the show.

articles.title: Coming out about my bipolar disorder has led to a new deep sense of community
articles.description: Dr. Devika Bhushan went public with her diagnosis to help dispel stigma. In the process, she says, she's forged bonds with hundreds touched by mental illness.

articles.title: The truth about teens, social media and the mental health crisis
articles.description: A striking decline in teen mental health has coincided with the rise of smartphones and social media. Is social media causing the mental health challenges? Finally, research can answer that question.

articles.title: Russia is draining a massive Ukrainian reservoir, endangering a nuclear plant
articles.description: Satellite data show water levels plummeting at the Kakhovka Reservoir. The reservoir supplies drinking water, irrigates vast tracts of farmland, and cools Europe's largest nuclear plant.

articles.title: Maternal deaths in the U.S. spiked in 2021, CDC reports
articles.description: After years of high rates, the country hit a new high during the pandemic, far exceeding rates in other developed nations. Black women are at especially high risk.

articles.title: 'I love selling out': Charli XCX on the volatile pop of 'Crash'
articles.description: On Charli XCX's Crash , the artist leans fully into a mainstream pop persona for the first time in almost a decade.

articles.title: A Taylor Swift Instagram post helped drive a surge in voter registration
articles.description: More than 35,000 new voters registered at Vote.org after the singer posted a link on her Instagram Stories. "I've heard you raise your voices, and I know how powerful they are," Swift wrote.

articles.title: QAnon supporters are promoting 'Sound of Freedom.' Here's why
articles.description: The movie is being criticized as a vehicle for conspiracy theories and misleading depictions of human trafficking — landing it in the middle of the country's politically polarized culture wars.

articles.title: The Supreme Court leaves Indian Child Welfare Act intact
articles.description: The case pitted prospective adoptive parents and Texas against the act, a federal law aimed at preventing Native American children from being separated from their extended families and their tribes.

articles.title: The 10 best jazz albums of 2023
articles.description: The best jazz albums of the year feel supercharged with the spirit of discovery, but also offer revelations — both comforting and challenging — the deeper you dig.

articles.title: Mystery recordings will now be heard for the first time in about 100 years
articles.description: The New York Public Library recently received a machine that will read cracked and scratched wax cylinders — which include some of the earliest recorded audio.

articles.title: 'Dreams do still come true' in a new novel by Dolly Parton and James Patterson
articles.description: Parton didn't just co-write the novel, she also recorded a whole album to go with it. Run, Rose, Run is about an aspiring country singer trying to shake a dark past and make it big in music.

articles.title: This 22-year-old is trying to save us from ChatGPT before it changes writing forever : Planet Money
articles.description: A college kid's mission to prevent misuse of artificial intelligence.

articles.title: Scanning students' rooms during remote tests is unconstitutional, judge rules
articles.description: In what's believed to be the first case of its kind, a student argued that Cleveland State University violated his Fourth Amendment rights when he complied with a webcam recording of his exam space.

articles.title: Tyler Childers is back, and taking chances
articles.description: The grassroots country star, whose fan base crosses lines of identity and politics, is releasing a song called "In Your Love," from a new album. Its video tells a queer, Appalachian love story.

articles.title: After years of early success, Omar Apollo releases full debut album 'Ivory'
articles.description: Ayesha Rascoe speaks with Omar Apollo about his psychedelically soulful music and his full-length album, "Ivory."

articles.title: 'Barbie' review: Sometimes corporate propaganda can be fun as hell
articles.description: Based on one of America's most emblematic pieces of intellectual property, Greta Gerwig's Barbie movie was never going to be just a movie, because Barbie was never just a doll.

articles.title: Demand at food banks is way up again. But inflation makes it harder to meet the need
articles.description: High food and gas prices are squeezing working families, sending some to food pantries for the first time. But providers are struggling with high costs, fewer donations and supply chain woes.

articles.title: Usher: Tiny Desk Concert
articles.description: The R&B goliath caps off our Black Music Month celebration, highlighting a catalog chock-full of hits spanning 25 years.

articles.title: The vast majority of criminal cases end in plea bargains, a new report finds
articles.description: The practice prioritizes efficiency over fairness and innocence, the American Bar Association says, and leads innocent people to be coerced into guilty pleas.

articles.title: In Dua Lipa's ever-expanding world, 'there's no time limit and there's no what-ifs'
articles.description: The pop star is returning to stages two years after releasing an acclaimed second album, Future Nostalgia , and being forced like everyone else to hunker down for the long chill.

articles.title: Petting other people's dogs, even briefly, can boost your health
articles.description: You don't even have to own one. Research shows just 5 to 20 minutes interacting with other people's pooches can reduce stress hormones and increase well-being.

articles.title: How Barnes & Noble turned a page, expanding for the first time in years
How comic Leslie Jones went from funniest person on campus to 'SNL' star
articles.description: Jones says performing stand-up for the first time as a freshman in college felt like putting on a shirt that fit perfectly: "It was just so natural." Her memoir is Leslie F*cking Jones.

articles.title: A top researcher says it's time to rethink our entire approach to preschool
articles.description: A long-term study of a statewide preschool program tracked students through the sixth grade and found those who attended prekindergarten falling behind.

articles.title: Study suggests that exposure to different smells could help improve memory
articles.description: A new study shows being exposed to different smells could help improve learning and memory. It also suggests that when we age, our sense of smell declines along with memory.

articles.title: Community college enrollment is down, but skilled-trades programs are booming
How bad is maternal mortality in the U.S.? A new study says it's been overestimated
Immigrants are less likely to commit crimes than U.S.-born Americans, studies find
Tiny Desk Playlist: Zazie Beetz and David Rysdahl's favorite Tiny Desk concerts
Pressed on his election lies, former President Trump cuts NPR interview short
articles.description: The former president blasted Republicans who have crossed him and kept up repeated election lies in an NPR interview.

articles.title: N.C. radio station reverses decision to withhold broadcast of contemporary Met operas
articles.description: WCPE had deemed operas dealing with race and LGBTQ issues "unsuitable" for broadcast. They reversed course "after careful deliberation...and hearing from our supporters, listeners and the public."

articles.title: Activist Judy Heumann led a reimagining of what it means to be disabled
articles.description: Heumann was instrumental in pushing to expand the civil rights of Americans with disabilities and continued to advocate for disability rights around the globe. She died on Saturday at age 75.

articles.title: A robot was scheduled to argue in court, then came the jail threats
articles.description: The man behind a startup called DoNotPay planned to use AI to help fight a traffic ticket. But professional lawyers shut it down.

articles.title: The best video games of 2023, sorted by genre and platform
articles.description: 2023 broke video game industry records, both in the quantity and quality of acclaimed, financially successful games. NPR staff and contributors bring you their favorites.

articles.title: With omicron, you need a mask that means business
articles.description: To block a variant this transmissible, scientists say you need an N95 or other high-filtration mask. Here's how to find a good one and when to wear it.

articles.title: Climate change makes wildfires in California more explosive
articles.description: A new study pins about 25% of the extra risk on human-caused climate change.

articles.title: Brian Stelter to depart CNN as it cancels 'Reliable Sources' media show
articles.description: CNN chief Chris Licht informed host Brian Stelter that Reliable Sources would be canceled after more than three decades on air amid a great level of cost-cutting at the network.

articles.title: The importance of religion in the lives of Americans is shrinking
articles.description: The importance of religion in the lives of Americans is on the decline. That's according to a new report from the Public Religion Research Institute.

articles.title: In 'Martyr!,' an endless quest for purpose in a world that can be cruel and uncaring
articles.description: Engaging and wildly entertaining, Kaveh Akbar's debut novel will undoubtedly be considered one of the best of the year because it focuses on very specific stories while discussing universal feelings.

articles.title: A secret shelf of banned books thrives in a Texas school, under the nose of censors
articles.description: A teacher at a public school near Houston has a secret classroom bookshelf largely made up of challenged titles. Many of the books deal with race, sex and gender.

articles.title: Netflix plans to open brick and mortar locations
articles.description: The streamer plans to open physical stores — dubbed Netflix House — offering retail, dining and content-themed entertainment. It's unclear if they'll sell DVDs.

articles.title: Want to support the people in Ukraine? Here's how you can help
articles.description: Several organizations are asking for assistance in helping people affected by the Russian invasion.

articles.title: In 2022, Black farmers were persistently left behind from the USDA's loan system
articles.description: An NPR data analysis shows Black farmers were accepted for USDA direct loans at a lower rate than other racial groups in 2022. Direct loans are supposed to be among the easiest for farmers to get.

articles.title: These companies tried a 4-day workweek. More than a year in, they still love it
articles.description: Most of the companies in a U.K. trial were so pleased with the results — improved wellbeing, lower turnover, greater efficiency — they've made the four-day workweek permanent.

articles.title: U.S. recovered non-human 'biologics' from UFO crash sites, former intel official says
articles.description: Lawmakers heard firsthand accounts of craft that are "beyond our current understanding of our technology," and allegations that the U.S. recovered non-human "bio remains."

articles.title: 1 in 4 Americans say violence against the government is sometimes OK
articles.description: In a new survey, both liberals and conservatives agreed violent protests are sometimes justifiable. Republicans were twice as likely as Democrats to say violence is justified "right now."

articles.title: What to know now that hearing aids are available over the counter
articles.description: The shift in hearing health care is due to a recent rule change by the FDA, which recently cleared the way for the devices to be sold in retail stores without the need for buyers to see a doctor.

articles.title: Affirmative action for rich kids: It's more than just legacy admissions : Planet Money
articles.description: A blockbuster new study finds that America's elite private colleges are systematically giving huge advantages to rich kids over their equally bright, yet less privileged peers.

articles.title: A tech billionaire is quietly buying up land in Hawaii. No one knows why
articles.description: A mystery has been brewing in a small ranching town on Hawaii's Big Island. Word has it that Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff bought the land, stirring worries about what he plans to do with it.

articles.title: Deepfake video of Zelenskyy could be 'tip of the iceberg' in info war, experts warn
articles.description: A fake video of the Ukrainian president claiming defeat spread on social media on Wednesday.

articles.title: Read NPR's full interview with former President Donald Trump
articles.description: NPR's Steve Inskeep spoke with former President Donald Trump on Tuesday. Trump continued to repeat false claims that the 2020 election was rigged.

articles.title: Why 2023 was the Year of the Girl
articles.description: 2023 saw an endless stream of trends signaling the popularity of "Girl Culture." NPR's Juana Summers speaks with writer Isabel Cristo about why adult women were so drawn to expressions of girlhood.

articles.title: Montana becomes 1st state to approve a full ban of TikTok
articles.description: Montana's bill goes farther than bans in nearly half of the states that target devices on state-issued devices. Instead, Montana's legislation makes it illegal for anyone to download TikTok.

articles.title: Russell Moore on 'an altar call' for Evangelical America
A librarian collects all the things left in books — from love letters to old photos
articles.description: The Oakland Public Library has spent years collecting items its patrons have left in library books, from old photographs to love notes. The archive is available publicly on their website.

articles.title: The cost of candy is up a scary 13% just in time for Halloween
Democrats passed a major climate, health and tax bill. Here's what's in it
The water crisis in Jackson follows years of failure to fix an aging system
articles.description: More than 150,000 people are without clean water. For years, aging infrastructure and a lack of investment left residents dealing with unreliable access and worries about the safety of the water.

articles.title: Sick and struggling to pay, 100 million people in the U.S. live with medical debt
articles.description: The U.S. health system now produces debt on a mass scale, a new investigation shows. Patients face gut-wrenching sacrifices.

articles.title: A kid's guide to climate change (plus a printable comic)
articles.description: Learning about climate change? Here's a comic for kids about what it is and how it's affecting the planet — as explained by kids who are experiencing it. And find out how to print this comic at home!

articles.title: Patrick Bringley on his book 'All the Beauty in the World'
articles.description: Patrick Bringley found solace and healing while working as a guard at New York City's Metropolitan Museum of Art. NPR's Scott Simon talks with Bringley about his book, "All the Beauty in the World."

articles.title: As a nurse faces prison for a deadly error, her colleagues worry: Could I be next?
articles.description: Former nurse RaDonda Vaught is on trial on charges of reckless homicide. Her case raises consequential questions about how nurses use computerized medication-dispensing cabinets.

articles.title: She was denied entry to a Rockettes show — then the facial recognition debate ignited
articles.description: When a lawyer was denied entry to a Rockettes show, it became a flashpoint in the debate over facial recognition technology. Does it keep people safe, or risk further harm?

articles.title: Researchers say time is an illusion. So why are we all obsessed with it?
articles.description: Even guardians of America's atomic clocks say time doesn't work the way we think it does.

articles.title: Logic is ready to do things his way
articles.description: In an interview with Morning Edition , rapper Logic explains the central message of his new album, Vinyl Days : "I rap good! Let's just be honest here."

articles.title: In Ethel Cain's music, hell is a place on Earth
articles.description: The artist's debut album Preacher's Daughter drives deep into the heart of gothic Americana.

articles.title: TikTok has changed music — and the industry is hustling to catch up
articles.description: TikTok has flipped the script on the music industry, and everyone from artists to analysts and even marketing bosses at the top labels are trying to catch up.

articles.title: The creator of 'Bluey' writes for both kids and grown-ups
articles.description: NPR's Juana Summers talks with Joe Brumm, creator of the hit TV series "Bluey," about the show's international success, which now has a theatrical adaptation "Bluey's Big Play."

articles.title: Emi Nietfeld is done reaching for redemption in 'Acceptance'
articles.description: The memoir is not a phoenix-rising-from-the-ashes tale. Instead, Nietfeld refuses silver linings and focuses on the toll of contorting oneself into a "perfect, deserving" victim.

articles.title: America, we have a problem. People aren't feeling engaged with their work
articles.description: A new Gallup report finds employee engagement in the U.S. fell in 2022 to 32%. Young people in particular reported feeling less cared about at work and having fewer opportunities to learn and grow.

articles.title: Is 'rainbow fentanyl' a threat to your kids this Halloween? Experts say no
articles.description: The Drug Enforcement Administration is warning that drug dealers are marketing rainbow-colored fentanyl to kids. Many drug experts say that's likely not happening.

articles.title: Poll: Majorities oppose Supreme Court's abortion ruling and worry about other rights
articles.description: 56% of Americans disapproved of the decision in an NPR/PBS NewsHour/Marist poll conducted after it was announced. A similar number say it was motivated by politics — not law.

articles.title: The ozone layer is on track to recover in the coming decades, the United Nations says
articles.description: The ozone layer is a thin shield in the stratosphere that protects humans and the environment from harmful levels of the sun's ultraviolet radiation.

articles.title: Bills targeting trans youth are growing more common — and radically reshaping lives
articles.description: An NPR analysis finds that over the past two years, state lawmakers introduced more than 300 bills targeting trans people. Most of this legislation, 86%, takes aim at the rights of trans youth.

articles.title: New Zealand considers changing its name to confront its troubled colonial past
articles.description: As the people of New Zealand confront their nation's troubled past with colonization, a return to the Maori name of Aotearoa is being presented to a parliamentary committee.

articles.title: He got an unexplained $250,000 payment from Google. The company says it was a mistake
articles.description: Sam Curry, a self-described hacker, was puzzled by the payment. A Google spokesperson says the company paid "the wrong party as the result of human error" and was working to correct it.

articles.title: Planned Parenthood mobile clinic will take abortion to red-state borders
articles.description: Planned Parenthood says it will provide abortions out of an RV-based clinic in southern Illinois by the end of the year. It will reduce travel time for some patients coming from surrounding states.

articles.title: Banned Books: Author George M. Johnson on the need to tell all people's stories
articles.description: Writer and LGBTQ activist George M. Johnson speaks about what's lost when books like their 2020 memoir All Boys Aren't Blue are banned from school libraries.

articles.title: With new guidance, CDC ends test-to-stay for schools and relaxes COVID rules
articles.description: Revised guidance from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention looks to minimize COVID-19's disruption of daily life while conceding that the pandemic isn't over.

articles.title: Black History Month 2024 has begun. Here's this year's theme and other things to know
articles.description: The annual celebration started out in 1926 as Negro History Week and expanded to Black History Month in the 1970s. This year celebrates "African Americans and the Arts."

articles.title: Russia's at war with Ukraine. Here's how we got here
articles.description: Since breaking from the Soviet Union, Ukraine has wavered between the influences of Moscow and the West, surviving scandal and conflict with its democracy intact. Now it faces an existential threat.

articles.title: Former Pentagon chief Esper says Trump asked about shooting protesters
articles.description: NPR's Michel Martin speaks with Mark Esper about his forthcoming book, "A Sacred Oath: Memoirs of a Secretary of Defense During Extraordinary Times."

articles.title: Those fake active shooter calls to schools? A similar thing happened before
articles.description: As schools across the U.S. are targeted by false calls about active shooters, NPR has found evidence that a similar scheme took place in the spring.

articles.title: Dyeing the Chicago River green is a St. Patrick's Day tradition. How did it start?
articles.description: For more than 60 years, Chicago has turned its downtown river green to celebrate St. Patrick's Day. The annual tradition actually has its roots in a big problem for the city: sewage.

articles.title: Musk's Twitter has dissolved its Trust and Safety Council
articles.description: The advisory group of nearly 100 independent civil, human rights and other organizations was formed in 2016 to address hate speech, child exploitation, suicide and other problems on the platform.

articles.title: A woodpecker's brain takes a big hit with every peck: study
articles.description: A new study refutes the popular idea that a woodpecker's brain is cushioned from the violent impacts of pecking. It offers a different reason the birds avoid brain damage.

articles.title: What we know about the killing of Tyre Nichols
articles.description: Body cam footage of the brutal arrest in Memphis of the Black man has sparked protests in several cities. The five ex-officers involved face a litany of charges, including second-degree murder.

articles.title: This 830-million-year-old crystal might contain life. And we're about to open it
articles.description: From lemons to ham, salt is a handy food preservative. But researchers studying some really old salt crystals found them preserving something else — evidence of life.

articles.title: Group aiming to defund disinformation tries to drain Fox News of online advertising
articles.description: A group of activists who have taken on some of the biggest right-wing personalities online have now launched a campaign to try to defund Fox News' online operation.

articles.title: The Arctic is heating up nearly four times faster than the whole planet, study finds
articles.description: The Arctic is very sensitive to climate change. In the last 40 years, the region has warmed much more rapidly than the Earth as a whole, a new study finds.

articles.title: This is the wild and opulent history of Mar-a-Lago, long before Trump and the FBI
What is May Day? For the most part, the opposite of capitalism
articles.description: What springs to mind when you hear May Day? In the U.S. and abroad, the day has grown to encompass a spectrum of meanings. But the themes have remained the same: worker unity, suppression and rebirth.

articles.title: Author Maia Kobabe: Struggling kids told me my book helped them talk to parents
articles.description: In 2020, Gender Queer was given a Stonewall Honor and an Alex Award and was headed for a fourth printing. By spring of 2022 it topped the ALA's list of most challenged books.

articles.title: Our roads are killing wildlife. The new infrastructure law aims to help
Americans are fleeing to places where political views match their own
articles.description: America is growing more geographically polarized — red ZIP codes are getting redder and blue ZIP codes are becoming bluer. People appear to be sorting.

Why experts say you shouldn't bag your leaves this fall
Racial bias affects media coverage of missing people. A new tool illustrates how

Millions of Americans have long COVID. Many of them are no longer working

27 school shootings have taken place so far this year
Supreme Court restricts the EPA's authority to mandate carbon emissions reductions

articles.description: Almost 1 in 10 nurses who were issued new licenses last year waited six months or more, an NPR analysis found. Nurses say patient care suffers as these delays make staffing shortages even worse.

articles.title: Entries We Love: Allison Mahal, 'Autopilot'
articles.description: Allison Mahal's soothing vocals are a bittersweet contrast to the melancholy of the song in her Tiny Desk Contest entry.

articles.title: You can now ask Google to take your personal data out of its search results
articles.description: Anyone who doesn't want their phone number, email or street address to be found online can ask Google to omit the data from its search results.

articles.title: A Texas team comes up with a COVID vaccine that could be a global game changer
articles.description: Peter Hotez and Maria Elena Bottazzi used an oldie-but- goodie technology to devise a vaccine that's easy to make — and relatively cheap. India has already ordered 300 million doses.

articles.title: Architect behind Googleplex now says it's 'dangerous' to work at such a posh office
articles.description: Clive Wilkinson says it's really not a good thing for employees to work at a place that has catered meals, private parks, massage tables and a laundromat ... because why would you ever leave?

articles.title: Yellowstone renames a mountain after the history of its prior namesake comes to light
articles.description: The country's first national park has opted to change the name after research uncovered the involvement of Gustavus Doane in an attack that killed 173 Native Americans.

articles.title: Free N95 masks are arriving at pharmacies and grocery stores. Here's how to get yours
articles.description: Some retailers are starting to get the first wave of the 400 million free masks being distributed by the federal government. Every person is allowed to receive up to three masks.

articles.title: Talib Kweli on Black Star's return: 'We stand tall on the shoulders of our ancestors'
articles.description: Talib Kweli discusses the return of Black Star after 24 years, including a return to some of the duo's foundational themes — black excellence, unity, Pan-Africanism and the raising of consciousness.

articles.title: This experimental drug could change the field of cancer research
articles.description: A small trial using the drug dostarlimab yielded an unprecedented success rate in eliminating tumors.

articles.title: Glaciers are shrinking fast. Scientists are rushing to figure out how fast
articles.description: Billions of people rely on glaciers for drinking water, hydropower and irrigation. A raft of new research suggests there is less ice left than previously thought.

articles.title: 'The Batman' review: Robert Pattinson shines in this back-to-basics approach
articles.description: Matt Reeves' approach to the venerable hero is more emo than goth, and Robert Pattinson brings a haunted quality to the role.

articles.title: Starbucks workers form their 1st union in the U.S. in a big win for labor
articles.description: Baristas and other workers from three stores voted whether to unionize. Starbucks fought the plan. Now

articles.title: Biden signs gun safety bill into law
articles.description: The president's signing comes just over a month after the mass shooting at an elementary school in Uvalde, Texas, killed 19 children and two adults.

articles.title: Raveena's galactic journey back down to Earth
articles.description: On her new album, Asha's Awakening , the artist Raveena sends her protagonist on a thousand-year intergalactic journey of discovery, all in order to better understand her own place on Earth.

articles.title: Americans are stuck in unhealthy pandemic habits. Here's how to reboot
articles.description: After two years of pandemic life, people have learned to cope in ways that have become stubborn, unhealthy habits. But there are positive steps we can take to reset a healthy lifestyle.

articles.title: Russia-Ukraine war worsens fertilizer crunch, risking food supplies
articles.description: The Russia-Ukraine war pushes up the price of natural gas, a key ingredient in fertilizer, and has led to severe sanctions against Russia, a major exporter of fertilizer.

articles.title: Why this 1990s McDonalds burger showed promise of being a wild success — but flopped
articles.description: The McDonald's Arch Deluxe is one of the most infamous product failures in history. In his new book, The Voltage Effect, economist John List says it's an example of a good idea failing to scale up.

articles.title: A timeline of the Jan. 6 Capitol attack — including when and how Trump responded
articles.description: Three years later, and as we begin an election year where Donald Trump is the clear frontrunner for Republican nomination, we revisit the events of that day — and exactly what happened when.

articles.title: U.S. COVID hospitalizations hit new record high, raising risks for patients
articles.description: There are more patients and, in some places, not enough health care workers to go around. Research shows the crowding will impact care and increase mortality for all patients.

articles.title: The military's UFO database now has info from about 400 reported incidents
articles.description: That's up from 143 incidents in a report issued in 2021. Officials partly credited reducing stigma around the issue for the new reports, many of which are older and went unmentioned at the time.

articles.title: Some white congregations are paying to use hymns written by enslaved African people
articles.description: Some white congregations are paying what they're calling "royalites" when they sing hymns that come from the Negro spiritual tradition. They say it's a matter of racial justice.

articles.title: The story behind Asian Pacific American Heritage, and why it's celebrated in May
articles.description: May marks the beginning of Asian American and Pacific Islander Heritage Month. This year's theme is Advancing Leaders Through Opportunity.

articles.title: 'Succession' co-star Kieran Culkin is having fun as Roman Roy
articles.description: Culkin plays one of three siblings vying for control of a media empire: "This guy grew up never having to suffer consequences, and so he doesn't really know what that means to suffer consequences."

articles.title: In Bucha, death, devastation and a graveyard of mines
articles.description: Images of dead civilians in the streets of Bucha shocked the world and intensified concerns of Russian war crimes in Ukraine. Officials want more military aid, and bigger consequences for Russia.

articles.title: Your dog is a good boy, but that's not necessarily because of its breed
articles.description: A new study based on thousands of DNA sequences and owner surveys finds that less than 10% of a dog's behavior — like howling, herding or retrieving — can be explained by its breed.

articles.title: Trailblazing feminist author, critic and activist bell hooks has died at 69
articles.description: The prolific author, poet, cultural critic, feminist and professor, who wrote more than three dozen wide-ranging books, died Wednesday at her home in Berea, Ky.

articles.title: Putin's claim of fighting against Ukraine 'neo-Nazis' distorts history, scholars say
articles.description: Scholars dismiss the Russian leader's claims as a "mythical use of history." For one: Ukraine overwhelmingly elected a Jewish president, and has a relatively small right-wing movement.

articles.title: Americans are deeply divided on transgender rights, a poll shows
articles.description: An NPR/Ipsos poll shows a stark partisan split on laws that prevent transgender youth from accessing medical care for gender transition.

articles.title: Blinken sets a standard for lifting sanctions: an 'irreversible' Russian withdrawal
articles.description: In an interview with NPR, Secretary of State Antony Blinken, the top U.S. diplomat, warns of the further devastation of Ukrainian cities.

articles.title: This is how many lives could have been saved with COVID vaccinations in each state
articles.description: A large share of the nearly 1 million people who died of COVID in the U.S. may have lived if they'd gotten vaccinated. A new analysis shows how many lives could have been saved across the country.

articles.title: Facebook, Google and Twitter limit ads over Russia's invasion of Ukraine
articles.description: The moves come as U.S. tech platforms are under pressure to take a stronger stance against Russia and limit disinformation.

articles.title: The original Roe v. Wade ruling was leaked, too
articles.description: Leaks of any kind are rare at the Supreme Court, but in 1973, the original Roe decision was leaked to the press before the court formally announced it. The chief justice was furious.

articles.title: What to know about Title 42, the Trump-era policy now central to the border debate
articles.description: A decades-old public health order is back in the spotlight as it's set to expire next month — a move that is long-overdue for immigration advocates. Here are some Title 42 basics, and some history.

articles.title: There's never been such a severe shortage of homes in the U.S. Here's why
articles.description: Home prices rose nearly 20% last year, in large part because the U.S. is several million homes short of demand. Builders say the pandemic is partly to blame, but the problem goes deeper than that.

articles.title: Data analysts proved what Black Pittsburgh knew about COVID's racial disparities
articles.description: Community leaders saw early in the pandemic that the city's residents of color were being hit hard by COVID-19. They worked with data analysts to show just how hard, where and why.

articles.title: Beloved creator of the GIF dies following complications from COVID, wife confirms
articles.description: Steve Wilhite, the creator of the GIF, died at age 74 due to complications from COVID-19.

articles.title: Halle Berry entered the ring ready — she's been a fighter all her life
articles.description: Berry stars as a disgraced MMA fighter in Bruised — a film she also directed. It's a role that she identifies with fundamentally: "I've also been a fighter my whole life, my whole career."

articles.title: From slavery to socialism, new legislation restricts what teachers can discuss
articles.description: Researcher Jeffrey Sachs says that U.S. teachers are being censored for broaching certain topics. One group in New Hampshire is offering a $500 bounty for teachers who discuss critical race theory.

articles.title: Rachel Levine calls state anti-LGBTQ bills disturbing and dangerous to trans youth
articles.description: The U.S. assistant secretary for health, who will speak at Texas Christian University, says physicians need to be more vocal in fighting politically motivated attacks on vulnerable trans youth.

articles.title: NASA scientists estimate Tonga blast at 10 megatons
articles.description: Researchers who have been studying the volcano since 2015 say it was likely caused by seawater flowing into a chamber filled with magma.

articles.title: No, you don't need to worry about joro spiders. They may even be helpful in some ways
articles.description: The palm-sized spider, which has been largely confined to the Southeastern states for nearly a decade, could soon colonize regions with colder climates to the north. But they're harmless to humans.

articles.title: DeSantis wants to end Disney World's special status in Florida
articles.description: Florida's Republican governor, Ron DeSantis, has asked lawmakers to consider a bill that would halt Disney World's exemptions to state regulations that were established more than 50 years ago.

articles.title: Thriller 'The Violin Conspiracy' addresses racism in classical music
articles.description: In his debut thriller, Brendan Slocumb employs polemic about racism to great effect as he reminds us that the high-toned world of classical music suffers from, and because of, racism.

articles.title: Former Theranos CEO Elizabeth Holmes to be sentenced on Sept. 26
articles.description: The onetime Silicon Valley star will remain free on a bond until her sentencing hearing. She faces the maximum possible penalty of decades behind bars.

articles.title: Newly published evidence points to Wuhan seafood market as pandemic origin point
articles.description: The studies offer the strongest evidence to date of a link between the animals at the seafood market and the spread of SARS-CoV-2. A top virus sleuth gives the details.

articles.title: A whiteness that's only skin deep : Code Switch
articles.description: We use words related to color to describe different racial categories all the time — Black, white, brown. But how much of race and identity actually has to do with the color of your skin? What if what appears to be "whiteness" is only skin deep? Today we're sharing stories from people of color with albinism whose experiences challenge what many people think they know about race.

articles.title: TikTok is driving book sales. Here are some titles #BookTok recommends
articles.description: BookTok — the world of book lovers on TikTok — is becoming a major force in the publishing industry.

articles.title: Alvin Lucier, inquisitive and innovative composer, has died at 90
articles.description: Lucier changed the way we think about sound through monumental works like I Am Sitting in a Room and Music on a Long Thin Wire .

articles.title: 'Morning Edition' host Noel King is leaving NPR
articles.description: Morning Edition hosts Noel King and A Martinez share news about Noel's new career opportunity.

articles.title: Accusations of 'greenwashing' by big oil companies are well-founded, a new study finds
articles.description: Chevron, ExxonMobil, BP and Shell used terms like "climate" and "low-carbon" more frequently in recent annual reports, but their actions on clean energy didn't match their words, researchers conclude.

articles.title: Want to be a better ally to disabled people? Here's how : Life Kit
articles.description: July is Disability Pride Month. Do you find yourself avoiding conversations on disabilities? A disability rights activist shares ways to be a better ally and to destigmatize disability in America.

articles.title: When Making Music Breaks Your Body
articles.description: An arthritis diagnosis means the latest album by the Bay Area band The Dodos is likely its last. It is a striking reminder of the oft-overlooked physical strains of music careers.

articles.title: The Debate About Pablo Escobar's Hippos : Short Wave
articles.description: Pablo Escobar had a private zoo at his estate in Colombia, with zebras, giraffes, flamingoes - and four hippopotamuses. After Escobar was killed in 1993, most of the animals were relocated except for the so-called "cocaine hippos." Authorities thought they would die but they did not and now, about a hundred roam near the estate. articles.title: Protections for gray wolves restored across much of the U.S.
articles.description: The ruling by a U.S. district judge puts a spotlight on a species whose recovery from near-extinction has been heralded as a historic conservation success.

articles.title: Millions of disabled Americans could lose federal benefits if they get married
articles.description: When Americans with disabilities get married they risk losing federal benefits. Momentum is building on Capitol Hill to change the rules.

articles.title: The Western megadrought is revealing America's 'lost national park'
articles.description: A famed desert landscape has reemerged as water levels in Lake Powell reservoir have fallen to record lows. It's raising questions about the future of this oasis and water in the American West.

articles.title: These NYC kids have written the history of an overlooked Black female composer
articles.description: A group of sixth, seventh and eighth grade students realized there was no children's book about the composer Florence Price. So they wrote, illustrated and published their own.

articles.title: 'Horizon Forbidden West' Review: a personal post-apocalyptic adventure
articles.description: A personal journey underpins a new video game about a post-apocalyptic American West reclaimed by nature and stalked by bestial robots.

articles.title: Therapy dogs can help relieve pain in the ER
articles.description: They have offered comfort at nursing homes, schools — even disaster sites. Now, a study shows that a 10-minute visit from therapy dogs can help relieve emergency room patients' pain.

articles.title: Incarcerated producer finds purpose in running a radio station from prison
articles.description: Inside Wire: Colorado Prison Radio is the first statewide prison radio station. NPR's Michel Martin talks to one of the producers at the Limon Correctional Facility.

articles.title: P.J. O'Rourke, author and 'Wait...Wait Don't Tell Me,' panelist, dies at 74
articles.description: O'Rourke authored more than 20 books, including Parliament of Whores and Give War a Chance, both of which reached #1 on the New York Times bestseller list.

articles.title: HBO's 'Euphoria' is more than a parent's worst nightmare. It's a creative triumph
articles.description: Euphoria's storytelling transcends the explicit themes its characters face.

articles.title: Kronos hack will likely affect how employers issue paychecks and track hours
articles.description: The attack affects several of its systems, including how employees track their paid time off and how they get paid, according to the company.

articles.title: NPR Music's 100 Best Songs Of 2021 (20-1)
articles.description: Think of the best songs of 2021 as a playlist catering to the most basic human urges. Within it, booties were called, muffins were buttered and bloody revenge was contemplated. It was quite a year.

articles.title: The 'Orbeez Challenge' is causing harm in parts of Georgia and Florida, police warn
articles.description: Police are warning their communities that a new TikTok challenge is taking off and causing harm in the process.

articles.title: Three ex-Minneapolis police officers guilty of violating George Floyd's civil rights
articles.description: A jury found that Thomas Lane, J. Alexander Kueng and Tou Thao all deprived Floyd of his right to medical care, and that two of them failed to intervene as Derek Chauvin knelt on Floyd's neck.

articles.title: 'In Defense of Witches' is a celebration of women
articles.description: Mona Chollet's book shows how women are still today expected to act certain ways or be ostracized, as it hails feminist minds — our modern witches — and their work.

articles.title: The truth in political advertising: 'You're allowed to lie'
articles.description: A campaign ad for Kari Lake, a Republican candidate for Arizona governor, includes baseless claims of a rigged 2020 election. Can candidates lie in their paid ads? The short answer: yes.

articles.title: 'Honor' is a searing meditation on the meaning of dignity in a dehumanizing world
articles.description: Thrity Umrigar's novel is about India's humanitarian crisis — with its depictions of misogyny and scenes of public shaming, mistreatment and torture — but it's also about a transformative journey.

articles.title: The U.S. tried permanent daylight saving time in the 1970s — then quickly rejected it
articles.description: The Senate this week voted with unanimous consent to adopt permanent daylight saving time hours to eliminate the need to change clocks twice a year.

articles.title: Better air in classrooms matters beyond COVID. Here's why schools aren't there yet
articles.description: Boosting ventilation and filtration not only lowers the risk of transmission, it's also linked to higher test scores and better health. But making upgrades is more complex than it sounds.
